newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-FALCONS FIRE COACH JUNE JONES.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-FALCONS FIRE COACH JUNE JONES.

text.p: June Jones joined the growing list of unemployed NFL head coaches on Monday after being fired by the Atlanta Falcons following a tumultuous 3-13 season.
Jones had guided the Falcons into the playoffs after the 1995 season, but Atlanta's 1996 campaign was marked by disappointment and turmoil.

"We all need to look at ourselves right now," Falcons president Taylor Smith said. "In no way is June Jones the sole reason this team finished 3-13. He took us to the playoffs last year and is, indeed, a talented coach and a quality individual."

Jones' season included the controversial release of starting quarterback Jeff George, prompted by a heated arguement between the two on the sidelines during a September 22 game against Philadelphia after Jones benched George.
The team appeared to become further divided when quarterback Bobby Hebert berated his offensive line while throwing six interceptions in a 34-27 loss to St Louis two weeks ago.

Jones' final game as Atlanta coach on Sunday ended in a way that seemed symbolic of the entire season when the usually reliable Morten Andersen missed a short field goal with four seconds left that would have given the Falcons a victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars. They lost 19-17.

Jones, a proponent of the Run-and-Shoot offence, was 7-9 in his first season in Atlanta and guided the team to a 9-7 mark and a wild-card playoff berth in 1995. He finished his first head coaching assignment with a 19-29 overall record.
Jones, a former backup quarterback with the Falcons, was a quarterbacks coach with the Houston Oilers and Detroit Lions before joining the Atlanta coaching staff in 1991 as an assistant.
The New York Jets, New York Giants and St Louis Rams also fired their head coaches as the 1996 season concluded.
